main_text.p: רָקִיעַ m. Expansum, cœli scil. in latum Diductio & Exten-sio, quod Græci dixerunt στερέωμα[?], Latini Firmamen-tum: Genef.1. v.6. Constr. רְקִיעַ הַשָּׁמָיִם Expansi cœlo-rum, verf.20. Hebrai septem firmamenta enumerant. Vide R.Salom. Psal.19.7.
רְקָעִים masc. pl. Diductiones: Constr. פִּחֵי רִקְעֵי[?] Diductiones bracteárum, Numer.17. v.3. id est, Laminas ductiles.

רָקַק[?] Spuere, Despuere, quod ab affini Verbo רָק mutatur. Futur. יָרֹק Despuerit, Levit.15. v.8. Ex Hiph. quidam deducunt, אֲרִיקֵם[?] Fricabo, Extenuabo eos, Psal.18.43. ut Dagesch in vocalem longam diductum fit. Aben Esra scribit, esse ex significato Nominis sequentis רְקוֹת Tenues. R.Salom. כְּטִיחַ הַנָּרוֹק שֶׁאֵינוֹ עָב[?] Sicut cæ-mentum tenue, quod non est crassum. Erit ergo רקק Attenuare, Tenue reddere, & Spuendi significatum ex Nomine efformatum. Vide supra in רִיק.
רָק m. Sputum, Saliva, Job.30.10. Aff. עַד בְּלְעִי רָקִי Donec deglutiam sputum meum, Job.7.19.
רַק Tantùm, Tantummodo, Duntaxat, particula Extenuandi, Genef.20.11. & 19.8. הָרַק אַךְ An tantummodo, duntaxat, Num.12.2. Pleonasmus ad magis extenuandum. Vide אַךְ.
רְקוֹת f. Tenuis; unde Plural. רְקוֹת בָּשָׂר Tenues carne, Gen.41.3. הַפָּרוֹת הָרְקוֹת Vacca tenues, v.20.
רָקָּה f. Tempus, pars capitis: Aff. רַקָּתוֹ Tempora ejus, Jud.5.26. בְּרַקָּתוֹ In tempora ejus, Jud.4.21.22.
רְקִיק m. Laganum, placenta tenuis, Exod.29.23. Plural. Construct. וּרְקִיקֵי מַצּוֹת Et lagana azymorum, id est, azyma, v.2.
רְשָׁיוֹן[?] m. Facultas, Licentia, Esf.3.7. pro quo Rabbini dicunt רְשׁוּת.

page.notes: Hebrew vowel points and some Greek and Hebrew letters in the large entry headings (רָקַק, רְשָׁיוֹן) and in the phrases marked [?] are not fully legible at this scan resolution; the marked forms are my best reading. The Greek word στερέωμα is doubtful. Printed "Esf.3.7." and "Pleonafmus" are copied as printed (the second with long s normalised to s). The Latin long s has been written as plain s throughout.
